newsitem.title: UK: IPE natural gas drought continues for fifth session.
newsitem.headline: IPE natural gas drought continues for fifth session.

text.p: The IPE natural gas contract was untraded on Tuesday afternoon -- the second complete day on which no trade has been done, and the fifth complete session.
The natural gas contract is open for two two-hour sessions each day. No trade has now been done since the morning session on Friday.
Physical traders said on Tuesday that there is a marked trend towards quiet mornings on both the physical and futures natural gas markets, with most deals getting done in the afternoon.
While Mondays used to be slow and the rest of the week busier, the tendency is increasingly for markets to be quiet every morning of the week.
But it is notable that IPE activity is not picking up in the afternoon sessions to reflect the increased level of business on the OTC market, traders said.
By the close there were bids posted for the first 10 months of the contract, although there were only offers for the four front months and for next February.

In front months June and July, bids were posted at 11.40 pence and 11.50 pence a therm respectively, above the previous settlement levels of 11.27 pence and 11.26 pence, and reflecting the current strength of the physical market.

But further out, bids fell below the settlement price with no corresponding offers posted except for February. This was bid at 17.65 pence against an offer at 18.00 pence, below the last settlement price of 18.18 pence a therm. But even though offers were sparse, the number of bids and offers on the screen was still greater than at the close of business on Monday.
